answers.answer:
CHANGE IN CLASSIFICATION (2.04 -> current 2.08)

In SCOPe 2.04 the two domains were not related at any level below class. The Clostridium histolyticum ColG collagen-binding domain (CBD) in 1nqd was d1nqda_ / d1nqdb_, SCCS b.23.2.1: fold b.23 'CUB-like' (SUNID 49853), superfamily b.23.2 'Collagen-binding domain' (SUNID 89260), family b.23.2.1 (SUNID 89261), protein 'Class 1 collagenase' (89262), species Clostridium histolyticum TaxId 1498 (89263). The Cry3A (CryIIIA/BT13) delta-endotoxin C-terminal domain in 1dlc was d1dlca1 (1dlc A:500-644), SCCS b.18.1.3: fold b.18 'Galactose-binding domain-like' (49784), superfamily b.18.1 (49785), family b.18.1.3 'delta-Endotoxin, C-terminal domain' (49796). Because b.23 and b.18 are distinct folds, 2.04 asserted no homology and not even a shared fold; the only common ancestor node was class b, 'All beta proteins' (48724), which carries no evolutionary claim.

In current SCOPe 2.08 the ColG CBD has been reclassified out of the CUB-like fold and into the Galactose-binding domain-like lineage. d1nqda_ (SUNID 86025) is now SCCS b.18.1.36: fold b.18 (49784) -> superfamily b.18.1 (49785) -> family b.18.1.36 'Collagen-binding domain' (SUNID 267607) -> protein 'Class 1 collagenase' (267633) -> species Clostridium histolyticum TaxId 1498 (267693). The old b.23.2 superfamily and b.23.2.1 family nodes no longer carry this domain, and the old SUNIDs 89260/89261 are not in the current lineage even though the domain SUNID 86025 is stable. d1dlca1 (SUNID 23719) is unchanged at b.18.1.3. Chain B was also re-partitioned in 2.08: the single 2.04 domain d1nqdb_ became d1nqdb1 (b.18.1.36, B:893-1008) plus d1nqdb2 (B:891-892), the latter placed in the artifacts class l.1.1.1 rather than in any true domain.

So the relationship moved from 'different fold, no implied relationship' to 'same superfamily, different families'. The deterministic comparison of d1nqda_ with d1dlca1 returns relationship = same_superfamily with lowest shared node b.18.1 (SUNID 49785) and the interpretation that a shared superfamily is consistent with probable common ancestry; no caveats are flagged on either domain. This is the SCOPe level reserved for probable but remote common ancestry inferred from structure and function rather than from sequence, which is exactly the right strength here: it is stronger than a mere fold match (which SCOPe treats as possible analogy, not homology) and weaker than the family level, where sequence identity or very clear functional equivalence would be required. They are NOT in the same family: b.18.1.36 versus b.18.1.3 remain separate, and they are not the same protein or species node.

STRUCTURAL EVIDENCE FOR COMMON ANCESTRY

1. Shared architecture. SCOPe's own fold description for b.18 is 'sandwich; 9 strands in 2 sheets; jelly-roll'. Both domains realize this lectin-like beta-sandwich jelly-roll topology, with the same strand count, the same two-sheet packing, and the same handedness of the roll. Agreement on strand order and crossing, not just on a generic beta-sandwich shape, is what distinguishes homology from convergence here and is the basis for pulling ColG out of the CUB-like fold; the CUB fold is also a beta-sandwich, so the 2.04 placement was a topology-level misassignment that superposition corrected.
2. Curator-cited literature. The current family node b.18.1.36 (SUNID 267607) carries the comment that PubMed 17977833 describes likely homology between d2quoa_, d1w99a3, and d1nqdb_ (the 2.04 SID for what is now d1nqdb1), with PubMed 17977833 recorded as the family cross-reference. The reclassification therefore rests on published structural-superposition evidence linking the ColG CBD to other members of the galactose-binding/lectin-like set, not on an automated sequence match.
3. Ligand-binding site placement. The CBD's collagen-binding surface and the carbohydrate-binding sites of canonical b.18.1 members lie on the equivalent edge/face of the sandwich, formed by loops emerging from the same ends of the same strands. Conserved site location on a conserved scaffold is independent evidence of descent.
4. Calcium. The 1nqd annotations record 'complexed with ca' for d1nqda_, and the entry itself is the CBD 3B structure solved in the presence of calcium; the bound Ca2+ rigidifies the sandwich and organizes the binding face. Metal-stabilized sandwich cores recur across this superfamily and are part of the shared structural signature.

FUNCTIONAL EVIDENCE FOR COMMON ANCESTRY

Both domains are non-catalytic accessory modules appended to a separate catalytic or active region of a large secreted bacterial protein, and both work by binding a polymeric or glycan-bearing target surface to confer substrate targeting. The ColG CBD is a C-terminal accessory module of a class I clostridial collagenase whose peptidase activity resides in a different, M9B-family catalytic region that is not present in 1nqd; the CBD anchors the enzyme to insoluble collagen fibrils and raises activity on the fibrillar substrate. Cry3A domain III is the C-terminal module of a three-domain delta-endotoxin: 1dlc itself is multidomain, with d1dlca3 (A:61-289, f.1.3.1) the membrane-targeting pore-forming region and d1dlca2 (A:290-499, b.77.2.1) the middle beta-prism/lectin-like domain, and d1dlca1 (A:500-644, b.18.1.3) contributes receptor and glycan recognition and specificity. The common functional theme, a lectin-like surface-adhesion module grafted onto an effector domain, is the kind of shared function SCOPe accepts alongside structure as superfamily-level evidence. The b.18.1.3 family is additionally mapped to Pfam PF03944, so the endotoxin side of the relationship has independent family-level sequence support within its own family, though that mapping does not extend across to the collagenase family.

LIMITS ON WHAT THIS LICENSES

- Superfamily, not family. Probable common ancestry is the claim; it is explicitly remote and is not detectable sequence similarity. SCOPe records homology_scope 'sf' for node 49785. There is no reported sequence identity between d1nqda_ and d1dlca1, and none should be asserted.
- No function transfer. b.18.1 spans galactose/carbohydrate-binding modules, collagen binding, and endotoxin receptor binding, so the specific ligand is family-level, not superfamily-level, property. Do not infer that Cry3A domain III binds collagen, that the ColG CBD has insecticidal or receptor-binding activity, or that either carries catalytic function. The ColG catalytic peptidase domain is absent from 1nqd, so 1nqd provides no catalytic-residue comparison at all, and the Cry3A pore-forming function belongs to d1dlca3 in a different class (f, membrane and cell surface proteins).
- Fold alone would be insufficient. Had the two only shared fold b.18, that would support an architectural resemblance consistent with analogy; the superfamily merge is what carries the ancestry claim. Conversely the 2.04 b.23 CUB-like placement shows that shared-sandwich intuitions are unreliable without superposition.
- Release dependence and identifier hygiene. Any statement about this pair must be release-pinned: b.23.2.1 is correct for 2.04 and wrong for 2.08, while b.18.1.3 is stable across both. The 2.04 SID d1nqdb_ no longer exists as such; cite d1nqdb1 for current work, and note the 2.08 l.1.1.1 fragment d1nqdb2 (B:891-892) is an artifact segment, not evidence.
- Representative and template caution. d1nqda_ is one CBD copy (chain A) of the CBD 3B construct solved with calcium at 1.65 A; the 1dlc endotoxin structure is a 2.5 A 1994 entry. Picking either as a modeling template for the other is inappropriate at superfamily distance: boundaries, loop conformations, and the metal site are not transferable, and domain partitioning in 1dlc must be respected rather than treating chain A as one unit.
- External evidence still required. Confirming the relationship beyond SCOPe's assertion needs the superposition and profile evidence in PubMed 17977833, independent structure-comparison output (for example FATCAT or DALI alignments between d1nqda_ or d1nqdb1 and d1dlca1), and profile-HMM or Pfam clan analysis bridging the collagen-binding and PF03944 families. Experimental support for the functional parallel requires binding assays specific to each family's own ligand; neither SCOPe record supplies such data.
